sentences.text:
This Criminal Petition is filed under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS') by the petitioner/accused No.2 seeking to quash the proceedings against him in Crime No.468 of 2023 on the file of Karimnagar Rural Police Station, Karimnagar Distrisct, for the alleged offences punishable under Sections 406 and 420 of the India Penal Code, 1860 (for short 'IPC').
2. Heard Mr. Mirza Azamath Ali Baig, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri Jithender Rao Veeramalla, learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondent No.1-State.
3.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the charge sheet is not filed against the accused No.2 and that he is not the father of the de-facto complainant and that he never received any gold ornaments as alleged by the prosecution and that accused No.1 is the father of the de-facto complainant.
He further submitted that no material was recovered from him.
Hence, he prayed the Court to quash the proceedings against the petitioner.

On the other hand, learned Additional Public Prosecutor opposed the submissions of the learned counsel for the petitioner stating that there are specific allegations against the petitioner and that the 41-A notice was issued to the petitioner however he has not replied to the said notice and he did not appear before the Police.
Hence, he prayed the Court to dismiss the petition.
5. Perused the record.
It is revealed that the petitioner herein is accused No. 2.

The material submitted by the learned Additional Public Prosecutor discloses that a notice under Section 41-A Cr.P.C. was duly served on the petitioner; however, the petitioner has failed to comply with the same.
It is further revealed that the petitioner had approached this Court through Crl.P. No. 8577 of 2024.

By order dated 01.08.2025, the petitioner was directed to appear before the Investigating Officer on or before 14.08.2025, and the Investigating Officer was directed to follow the procedure prescribed under Section 41-A Cr.P.C.
Despite these directions, the petitioner did not appear before the Investigating Officer and continues to remain absconding, while his whereabouts are not known.
A copy of the said order has also been filed along with the present petition.
The investigation is still pending.
In view of the above, no further orders are required to be passed and it is apparent that the petitioner is not entitled to any relief.
Accordingly, the criminal petition is dismissed.
